pages.x: When the last French king of the old line died in 1328, Edward III of England, his nephew through his mother, had a claim to the throne. The French chose Philip of Valois instead. In 1337 Philip seized Edward's lands in Gascony, Edward claimed the French crown, and the war began.

In 1346 an English army turned at bay at Crécy, in northern France. Thousands of English longbowmen, each able to shoot ten or more arrows a minute, cut down charge after charge of French knights. The blind King John of Bohemia had himself led into the fight, and died.

Edward's son, the Black Prince, won again at Poitiers in 1356 and captured the French king, John II, who was held in London for a ransom of three million gold crowns. Bands of soldiers out of work plundered the French countryside for years.

After years of truces and raids, Henry V invaded in 1415. At Agincourt his tired, sick army stood between two woods on a muddy field. The French knights in heavy armour floundered in the mud, and the archers shot them down. Henry married the French king's daughter, and their son was to rule both kingdoms.

In 1429, with Orléans under siege, a peasant girl of 17, Joan of Arc, came to the uncrowned Charles VII saying that the voices of saints had sent her to save France. Riding with the army, she broke the siege in nine days and led Charles to be crowned at Reims.

In 1430 Joan was captured by the Burgundians, allies of the English, and sold to them. A church court found her guilty of heresy, partly for wearing men's clothes, and she was burned alive at Rouen in 1431, aged 19. A later court cleared her, and in 1920 she was made a saint.
The war ended with gunpowder. France built up the best artillery in Europe, and its cannon battered down the walls of English-held towns and castles.
pages.fx: At Castillon in 1453 French guns shattered the last English army in France. The age of knights and castles was drawing to a close.

pages.x: After 116 years England had lost everything in France but Calais. The long war helped turn both lands into nations: English replaced French as the language of England's rulers, and France found a national heroine in Joan of Arc.
pts: Joan of Arc turned the tide
